**Solution 2 is the correct one.** The ratio is $r$.

Solution 1 is wrong. The inclusion $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))\subset S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$ is only the first step. At higher level there are additional old forms obtained from $f$ by the $\wp$-power degeneracy operators, and these contribute further copies of the same finite-slope eigensystem. Its claim that the $\alpha$-eigenspace is one-dimensional for all $r$ does not hold in the relevant setting.

Solution 3 is an unjustified guess. Its exponent $2D(r-1)$ comes from heuristic counting of Borel-type cosets and character contributions, with no argument that these reproduce the multiplicity. It also contradicts the $r=1$ normalization only in form, not in content, so it is not verified.

For Solution 2, I could not check the precise theorem from memory, so this rests on recollection of Hattori's results on finite-slope multiplicities at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$, plus a local heuristic. In the local representation at $\wp$, the $K_1(\wp^r)$-fixed vectors of an unramified principal series have dimension growing linearly in $r$, and the finite-slope part of the eigensystem $\lambda$ picks up one copy per level step. That gives multiplicity $r$ times the level-$\wp$ multiplicity, so the ratio is $r$.

CHOICE: 2
